sources.entry: agentcairn by ccf - Long-term, cross-project memory for AI coding agents. Your own Obsidian vault as the source of truth. Daemonless and without opaque databases, your memory belongs to you.

summary.one_liner: agentcairn is a local, Markdown-first long-term memory layer that lets multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes Agent and others) share one Obsidian-compatible vault, with a disposable DuckDB index for recall.
summary.what_it_does: It captures durable context from supported coding agent tools, stores it as inspectable Markdown notes with frontmatter, provenance and [[wikilinks]], and recalls the most relevant pieces when another agent asks. Recall fuses BM25 and semantic vector search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, with optional reranking and fallback to BM25 when a model fails. Notes carry validity fields (valid_from, valid_until, superseded_by) so superseded facts stay visible but rank lower. It can import Claude Code's auto-memory files (MEMORY.md and topic files) into the vault, and a sweep command reads supported transcript stores as a backstop capture. Embeddings run locally by default, with Voyage, OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic options that send redacted text off-machine when enabled. A companion agentcairn-obsidian plugin reads the same files.
use_cases: Give coding agents long-term memory across projects
Share one memory vault between Claude Code, Codex and other agents
Recall past decisions or bug fixes in a new agent session
Keep agent memory as plaintext Markdown viewable in Obsidian
Import Claude Code auto-memory into a shared store
Schedule background capture of agent transcripts
how_to_run: cairn recall "how did we fix the auth bug?" --vault ~/agentcairn
notable: Markdown vault is canonical; the DuckDB index is a rebuildable cache and can be deleted without losing memory
Hybrid BM25 + vector retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion and optional cross-encoder reranking
Time-aware corrections via valid_from, valid_until and superseded_by instead of silent overwrites
Preview-first installer (cairn install) with backup-first MCP config writes
No required daemon, external database or telemetry; local by default
caveats: Project is beta; the first local model load can be slow
Vault is plaintext by design; redaction is best-effort and file permissions are the main access control
Ambient capture varies by host: Cursor and Antigravity rely on out-of-band sweep; some MCP hosts have no lifecycle hooks
Scheduled automation targets only macOS launchd and Linux user crontab; other systems need a manual scheduler
